exposure: method of niche detection (transvaginal sonography vs. uterine tissue samples)
outcome: prevalence of internal, external, and bidirectional niches
niche measurements (height, residual myometrial thickness, adjacent myometrial thickness)
discrepancies in niche detection and measurement between ultrasound and tissue samples
cohort: The study included 200 patients with a prior cesarean delivery who were undergoing hysterectomy due to abnormal uterine bleeding.
finding: Niches were highly prevalent (91% in tissue samples), often detected via sonography but with notable discrepancies in measurements and detection rates compared to uterine tissue samples, and can form after a single cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Niche formation, a consequence of cesarean delivery, was found to occur after a single cesarean delivery and is linked to reduced residual myometrial thickness and increased future pregnancy complications.
cross-section timing: at the time of hysterectomy, comparing pre-hysterectomy sonography with post-hysterectomy tissue analysis
